text:
Muscle lactate production increases when glycolytic flux (pyruvate production) outpaces the mitochondria's ability to oxidize pyruvate and reoxidize NADH. This happens during high-intensity exercise, hypoxia or limited oxygen delivery, and high ATP demand, so lactate dehydrogenase converts pyruvate to lactate to regenerate NAD⁺. In short, it rises with intense or anaerobic exercise.

CONFIDENCE: 62
